chunks: And from him, from Ahmad, from Abdul Malik bin Utba, from Is'haq bin Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'Can one give a man eighty dirhams from the zakat?' He said, 'Yes, and increase it.' I said, 'Can I give him a hundred?' He said, 'Yes, and enrich him, if you are able to enrich him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of zakat to give and is it better to give more?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that while eighty dirhams serves as a baseline for zakat distribution, the primary objective is to elevate the recipient out of poverty, encouraging the giver to provide sufficiency if capable. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on zakat as a tool for economic empowerment rather than mere almsgiving, aligning with the principle of 'Ighna' (enrichment). The hadith underscores the flexibility in zakat amounts based on the recipient's needs and the giver's capacity, reinforcing the social welfare aspect of the obligation.
